summary: Confirmed DONE. In 60633eff3 (#710), loadPackagedBackendAppWindow got a gate (resolveBackendAppWindowAction). After a crash-restart, a window that already reported a usable shell on the backend origin gets an in-place reconnect nudge (SYSTEM_RESUMED_CHANNEL) and keeps its route. loadURL(backendHttpUrl) now runs only from the boot page, about:blank, or a backend-origin document that never became usable. The client deadlines the proposal depended on are in place: fetchWithDeadline (5 s), transient retry for ws-token/session (15 s), and the server httpStartupGate. Production desktop-main.log shows the shell-usable report arriving on every launch, so the gate is live, not dormant. The optional version check was not implemented; it is moot because a crash-restart relaunches the same bundled binary. One small missed edge: a renderer whose process died keeps its usable mark and is nudged instead of reloaded.

evidence.note: Pure gate. Returns load for an empty URL, about:blank or the boot URL. Returns ignore at bound or for another origin. Otherwise returns reconnect when shellUsable is true and load when it is false. Unit tests in backendAppWindowLoad.test.ts:23 cover the deep-route reconnect, the unusable reload, foreign origins and bound vs ready.

loadPackagedBackendAppWindow now resolves the action first. The reconnect branch (1741-1745) only calls notifyRenderersToReconnect() and returns. The only remaining loadURL(backendHttpUrl) in this path is at 1757. At f1be4abc7 the function called loadURL for any backend-origin URL.

The DESKTOP_STARTUP_MARKS IPC adds the sender to appShellUsableContents (declared at 495). The preload observer (startupMarks.ts) reports only after the primary-shell-usable mark, which service.ts:236 sets once the primary shell snapshot is applied. ~/.ryco/userdata/logs/desktop-main.log contains desktop.window.app.shell-usable on every recent launch.
The usable mark is cleared on every main-frame cross-document navigation start. Error pages and new documents must report again before they count as reconnectable.

reconnectAfterResume forces reconnect() on connections whose heartbeat is not fresh. It is skipped in hosted mode (1244-1246), so the new trigger does not bypass hosted lifecycle ownership. A connection whose last pong is under 15 s old (Effect pings every 8 s) is skipped. It then relies on the transport retry: the URL provider polls ws-token every 500 ms (primaryAuth retryTransientBootstrap) and the startup gate holds that request until the backend serves. The WebSocketConnectionCoordinator stall detector is the backstop.

The ws-token request runs through fetchWithDeadline (CONTROL_PLANE_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS = 5000, fetchWithDeadline.ts:11), with transient retry on refused, timeout and 502-504 (118-137). The POST that used to hang across the restart, and that the reload used to rescue, is now bounded.

The bootstrap token and port are fixed per app run, and the session signing secret is persisted (ServerSecretStore). The renderer's cookie session survives a backend crash-restart, so reconnecting in place needs no re-auth.
The render-process-gone handler only marks the load request failed. It does not remove the webContents from appShellUsableContents, so a dead renderer still counts as reconnectable.

fixDefects: Minor edge-case regression. The render-process-gone handler (apps/desktop/src/main.ts:4591-4596) sets request.failed but leaves the webContents in appShellUsableContents. getURL() still returns the backend-origin app URL. If the renderer process has died (OOM, GPU or renderer crash) when a backend crash-restart reaches readiness, resolveBackendAppWindowAction returns "reconnect" and notifyRenderersToReconnect sends IPC to a dead renderer. The window stays blank until the user presses Cmd+R. Before #710 the unconditional loadURL revived it. Not a blocker: it needs a renderer crash plus a backend crash-restart, and View > Reload is available. Not fixes, just notes: (a) the proposal's optional server-version check was not built; it only matters if files on disk change under a running app, such as a Linux deb/rpm upgrade, and the existing version-mismatch hint covers that. (b) The reconnect nudge skips a connection whose heartbeat is still fresh; the transport's own retry plus the startup gate reconnect at readiness.
implementationSketch: In apps/desktop/src/main.ts, inside the window.webContents.on("render-process-gone", ...) handler (around line 4591), add appShellUsableContents.delete(window.webContents) so a dead document is no longer reconnectable. Belt and braces: in loadPackagedBackendAppWindow (around line 1732), pass shellUsable: appShellUsableContents.has(contents) && !contents.isCrashed(). Then readiness takes the "load" path and loadURL(backendHttpUrl) revives the renderer. To make this testable, pull the check into a small helper, e.g. isReconnectableAppShell({ usable, crashed }), in backendAppWindowLoad.ts. Add a case to backendAppWindowLoad.test.ts: a deep backend-origin route with shellUsable false (crashed) resolves to "load". Optional and low value: send a distinct backend-restarted reason, or force reconnect of only the primary connection regardless of heartbeat freshness, so a crash shortly after a pong does not wait on the transport's retry timing. Validate with focused vitest runs for apps/desktop (backendAppWindowLoad.test.ts) and a manual check: kill the backend child and the renderer process (kill -9) in a packaged build, then confirm the window reloads.
decisionReason: Desktop-local window lifecycle only. No auth, E2EE, hosted lifecycle (supervision skips hosted mode) or Hub protocol change.
correction: Status is right. The auditor missed one small edge: render-process-gone does not clear appShellUsableContents, so a crashed renderer is treated as reconnectable and loses the reload that used to revive it after a backend crash-restart.
